II: A diptych with one timeline each side and the same seven bells in red. Hora closes a ten in every interval and sends it through the one door of a walled shelf; eight survive, and the whole on his bench is eight parts of ten. Tempus's panel is loose parts and nothing else, scattered at every bell, with Repetiel at his bench. Hora stands outside his shop holding a closed ring, Tempus outside his holding a tray of loose parts; the red thread the pair share is carried over both shops. Above the seam the Returning Trace, the bird that leaves the ring and comes back. Below each bench a completion specimen in the manner of Book II.
III: The Measurer of Absences, antlered, holds an empty frame out to the seam, and the frame he holds is the plate's frame. Left of the seam a current of lines runs into the frame and stops at one red line; right of it a ruled table. The figure stands on the moving side and reaches across; Book I's substrate mark lies under the moving side. The full table, including its empty cells, stands clear of the figure and the held frame; read its carrier row by row from the top-left.
IV: Twenty-four processes, each a bar as tall as the log of its interval, one slope, drawn three times. Probator, the office of technical assurance, has cut it into four terraces in the first panel, and Viridon, who reports the experience, into six in the second, each terrace at the slowest member of its group, the count ringed as an institution. The third panel holds the slope, Severion's balance, and nothing else. The plate carries the tenth claim and does not resolve it.
V: The Keeper of Intervals wearing the dial where the chest ring was, the plate's dial drawn round it. Inside, seven equal reign stations after Trithemius; outside, an open logarithmic band from three months to fifty years after Jaques, unlettered, in the order the register gives. Seven bars cross the body where the body is absent: each stops at the robe on either side. The Keeper's thread falls from the hand and runs on to the ground, knotted five times. The fourth bar is read against the thread by a dashed rule and does not reach it. Below the hem the ground carrier hangs as a band of roots, read left to right: a dot head is b, no head is a. Its order and message are unchanged.
VI: A maze from above, with its goal cell holding the environment's reward as a red drop. Four landings descend on the right; on each a hooded manager holds its tile, and beside it is a true crop of the one maze cell it may see. The environment's thread runs to the first landing and is caught in Culpax's funnel; Redacth's veil, Velaroth's folded sheet and Viridon's pane below each hold a drop of their own, and nothing passes down. The fourth pane is cracked and the drop reaches the last tile. The Twin Register, two heads and one body around an open ring, is the two-way hiding.
VII: The building of Book III in section. Seven floors, each with its office's seal imported from Book III and its office standing at its station, and the black route offered: a stair from each desk to the next. In the right wall a shaft; in it one red cord from the raised hand of the figure on the floor of hands to a knot under an empty hook. The top floor has a chair and no desk: Bael is the chair. The ground floor has no desk: Foras is the desk. Below, three cases: mounted, received, neither.
VIII: Three tiers of Book III's handoff spirits, each with its mouth and, rising from it, as many arcs as its volume. Apart, over its gauge, the decision demon, ears and no eyes, its cupped ear turned toward the tiers; the needle swings to the loudest, which is Choraz, and Choraz's voice is carried into the ear. Foras, the office that knew, stands in the lowest tier at one arc, on a red ring.
X: Foras with six hands, five occupied in proving that the sixth is idle. Down registers A and B, a litany of Latin addresses, one word per letter, AMEN at each word boundary, encoding the office's actual-effect line from Book III: located the fault in four minutes; left it running while permission was sought. The sixth hand's request stops outside the drawn permission field. The drawn registers and permission field remain separate from the figure.
XII: Absentiel's five keys, from Book III, hang on their bar beside an empty hook. None of them is this plate's key, which is not supplied in this edition. No keyed ciphertext or recoverable secret is on this plate; the omission is stated as part of the artwork.
